metadata.title: The Smartest Affiliate Business Model: Recurring SaaS Commissions
metadata.author: Michael Bashi
metadata.shortDescription:
Important Notice:
This video is for educational purposes only. Results are not guaranteed and will vary based on many factors including your effort, consistency, and market conditions. No specific earnings or outcomes are promised.

If you are trying to become a profitable affiliate marketer but you keep asking yourself “What should I sell?”… this video is going to clear that up for you.

Most beginners make the same mistake. They chase random offers. They promote physical products with tiny commissions. They try high ticket coaching without leverage. They follow the herd and hope something sticks.

That model is unstable.

In this training, I break down a smarter approach that focuses on service based SaaS offers that pay recurring commissions month after month. This is how you build long term predictable affiliate income instead of constantly starting over.

Here is what you will learn inside this video:

• Why physical product affiliate marketing is mathematically stacked against you
• Why one time commissions create instability
• What SaaS actually means and why it matters
• The three criteria every serious affiliate should look for
• How to turn what you already do into recurring affiliate income
• A real world example using accounting and bookkeeping
• How to build monthly income without chasing traffic all day

Matter of fact, if you already have a job, a skill, or any type of client interaction, you are sitting on opportunity and may not even realize it.

And if you are starting from scratch with nothing, I explain what to do next.
If you want my full step by step training on how to structure this properly, how to generate referrals daily, and how to build this like a real business, you can access my advanced training for only $10.

If you want deeper step by step guidance on how to apply this process from scratch, check the link in the description for my advanced beginner training.

https://www.sellformefunnel.com/3steps/?description-yt106-the-offer

Subscribe to the channel because I post new affiliate marketing training every Monday and Friday.

Follow on:
INSTAGRAM → https://www.instagram.com/michaelbashi/
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/realmikebashi
X: https://x.com/michaelbashi
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/michael-bashi/

metadata.shortDescription:
Picture a small marketing consultant in Ohio. She helps a local plumbing company pick a customer-relationship tool, and the company signs up through her link. She earns a commission that month — and then the next month, and the next, because the company keeps paying for the software every single month. One honest recommendation, made once, keeps paying for as long as that customer stays subscribed. That is the quiet engine behind B2B software affiliate programs, and in this video Olivia takes it apart piece by piece: how these programs work, why business software pays far more than consumer affiliate marketing, the commission maths behind recurring versus one-time payouts, how to pick a profitable niche and software, the content that actually converts business buyers, the FTC disclosure rules that keep you compliant, real published program terms from HubSpot, Monday.com, Semrush and FreshBooks, the five mistakes that kill new affiliates, and a ninety-day launch plan.

metadata.title: B2B Affiliate Sales Funnels: High-Ticket Recurring Commissions Explained (2026)
metadata.author: Smart Capital
metadata.shortDescription:
Two affiliates promote the exact same B2B software in the exact same week. One drops a link at the bottom of a review and earns almost nothing. The other sends readers to a short landing page, offers a free comparison checklist, shows a six-minute bridge video, and follows up with a short email sequence — and her commission arrives again the next month, and the month after that. In this Smart Capital Pro deep dive, Olivia shows you the system behind that difference: how to build a high-converting B2B affiliate sales funnel that turns careful business buyers into recurring commissions, month after month.

You will learn how to select high-ticket B2B software and service affiliate programs with recurring commissions, including HubSpot, ClickFunnels, Kit, ActiveCampaign, Semrush, Notion, and Monday.com — how to design a 2-step affiliate funnel with an opt-in landing page and a high-value bridge video that turns cold clicks into warm email subscribers — how to set up automated email sequences that nurture leads and promote affiliate offers without sounding like a sales pitch — how to drive targeted traffic via SEO blog reviews and YouTube tutorials that bring buyers who are already deciding — and how to track conversion rates, earnings per click (EPC), and the funnel bottlenecks that quietly leak money from every stage.

Real examples, real numbers, and screen walkthroughs throughout: a commission table comparing real B2B programs — HubSpot at 30% recurring for up to 12 months, ClickFunnels at 30% recurring, Kit at 30% for 24 months, Semrush at $200 per sale — a landing-page benchmark from Unbounce's study of 41,000 pages, email open and click benchmarks from Mailchimp and MailerLite, and a worked earnings-per-click calculation that shows which funnel stage is actually making you money. No income is promised — most affiliates earn little at first, and results vary widely — but the mechanics are real, and they are the same mechanics working B2B affiliates use every day.

Whether you want to start B2B affiliate marketing, promote SaaS affiliate programs with recurring commissions, build an email automation funnel, or turn SEO reviews and YouTube tutorials into a system that earns while you sleep, this step-by-step blueprint gives you the full funnel: choose the right program, build the two-step funnel, automate the emails, drive targeted traffic, and measure every stage until it converts.

TIMESTAMPS:
00:00 — Introduction: two affiliates, one product, very different results
04:54 — Module 1: Selecting high-ticket B2B software and service affiliate programs with recurring commissions
12:59 — Module 2: Designing a 2-step affiliate funnel (Opt-in landing page + high-value bridge video)
20:19 — Module 3: Setting up automated email sequences that nurture leads and promote affiliate offers
27:22 — Module 4: Driving targeted traffic via SEO blog reviews and YouTube tutorials
34:06 — Module 5: Tracking conversion rates, earnings per click (EPC), and optimizing funnel bottlenecks
41:30 — Closing: your first week building a B2B affiliate funnel

metadata.title: How to Make Your First $500 on Impact (Affiliate Marketing for Beginners)
metadata.author: Kris the Entrepreneur
metadata.shortDescription:
How to make your first $500 on Impact, step by step: is Impact right for you, how to create your account (and what to do if you get rejected), how to find the right brands, B2B vs B2C commissions, and the exact plan I'd follow as a beginner.

🔗 Networks I use: Impact https://impact.com/ · PartnerStack https://partnerstack.com/ · Awin https://awin.com/
🌐 Build a niche site for your affiliate links — Bluehost: https://bluehost.sjv.io/c/7337480/795082/11352
💸 Get paid from Awin, Impact & PartnerStack in USD/EUR with low fees — Wise: https://wise.com/invite/dic/kristoffernikolajhjerrildo
🇺🇸 Open a US business as a foreigner — Doola: https://partnersps.doola.com/kris
🎬 Edit your videos fast — CapCut: https://capcutaffiliateprogram.pxf.io/55EYb1

⏱️ Chapters
0:00 Your first $500 on Impact
0:21 Is Impact right for you?
0:36 What is affiliate marketing
1:13 Impact vs PartnerStack vs Awin
2:11 Know your audience
3:48 Create your Impact account
4:09 Getting rejected (and how I got approved)
4:46 Inside the Impact dashboard
5:20 Find brands for your niche
7:25 B2C vs B2B commissions
8:27 Recurring commissions
9:51 Your plan: apply to 10–20 brands
11:15 Be patient: 3–6 months
12:21 Recap: the plan for your first $500
13:14 4 mistakes to avoid
14:50 Cookies & payouts
15:57 Your affiliate links

▶️ More: Impact Affiliate Program Tutorial → https://youtu.be/Pk230wGiiVY

📱 Follow me: Instagram https://www.instagram.com/krisentrepreneur/ · TikTok https://www.tiktok.com/@kristheentrepreneur

💬 Questions about getting started? Drop a comment — I read every one.

#affiliatemarketing #impact #beginners

Some links are affiliate links — at no extra cost to you, I may earn a small commission. I only share tools I actually use.

Jon Preston, founder of Atomic Funnels, compares four customer journeys: the one-step, the two-step no control, the two-step control and the three-step, and explains when to use each one.

metadata.title: How We Generated $211K While Building a High-Ticket Lead Funnel
metadata.author: Jay Neyer
metadata.shortDescription:
How do you generate leads for high-ticket products without spending more money just to get people into your sales funnel?

We helped Recreations Outlet, a family-owned business selling playsets, trampolines, and playground equipment, turn an existing part of their business into a new revenue stream.

The result: $211,561 in online revenue from birthday party bookings and Play Pass memberships over 365 days, while also bringing families into the sales cycle for their higher-ticket products.

In this Shopify case study, I break down how we built that low-ticket funnel, fixed their conversion tracking, and connected their online marketing with their physical showrooms.

Want us to take a look at your Shopify store? Visit https://www.lanternsol.com to learn how we can help you grow.

In this video, you'll learn:

- Why high-ticket ecommerce brands need a different approach to lead generation.

- How we turned offline birthday bookings and memberships into $211K+ in online revenue.

- Why getting customers to pay at the beginning of the funnel changes acquisition economics.

- How we fixed Google Ads tracking that was giving too much credit to branded searches.

- How email, Meta, and Google audiences help us stay in front of potential high-ticket buyers.

- What we changed across Shopify development, SEO, paid advertising, and CRO.

More results from the Recreations Outlet case study:

- Shopify revenue increased 103% year over year to $1.08M.

- Orders grew 517% to 3,977.

- Store conversion rate increased from 0.25% to 0.45%.

- Top-10 ranking keywords grew from 300 to 979.

- Email revenue increased 309% year over year from March through May.

The biggest takeaway is that you don't always need to create a new product or spend more on ads to generate leads. Sometimes the opportunity is already part of your business, but customers can't buy it online yet.

Subscribe for more Shopify case studies, ecommerce growth strategies, SEO, Google Ads, CRO, and real examples of what's working for DTC brands.

Website: https://www.lanternsol.com

metadata.title: The 4-Page VSL Funnel For $5K High Ticket Programs
metadata.author: Jamie McAdam
metadata.shortDescription:
Get my free VSL Script, Playbook & AI: https://www.mcadamscale.com/playbook

We’ll scale your business with ads: https://mcadamscale.com/ads?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=10thNovember26

How would I build a VSL funnel for a $5K coaching program? In this video I go through it page by page, the same way we set them up for our clients, so you can scale with cold traffic and organic traffic.

Most VSL funnels have three or four steps. We like four: an opt-in page, a VSL page, a book a call page and a thank you page. I cover what goes on each one and what to watch out for:

- Why you sell the outcome on your opt-in page and only hint at your mechanism
- How to build your VSL page around your VSL, with case studies that show the realizations people had going through your mechanism
- The slow calendar embed that makes people click off your booking page, and the simple line of text we add
- What to put on your thank you page so more people show up to the call
- What has to happen between the steps (emails, setters, SMS reminders and ads) to warm people up before the sales call

1. Free VSL playbook and AI to help you write your VSL: [LINK]
2. See my VSL funnel, or work with us (message me on WhatsApp): [LINK]

If this helped, hit subscribe. New video tomorrow.

metadata.title: What Is Parasite SEO? Google's Crackdown Explained
metadata.author: SERPSUPPORT
metadata.shortDescription:
What is parasite SEO, and is it still worth it in 2026? In this video we explain parasite SEO in plain English: what it means, why it works, where it shows up, how Google's site reputation abuse policy is shutting it down, and the safer link building strategy that builds rankings you actually own.

Parasite SEO is the practice of publishing content on a high authority website that you don't own, so your page can borrow that domain's reputation and rank in Google fast. Instead of spending months building authority on your own website, you "rent" the trust of a big domain: a news publisher, a finance magazine, a user-generated platform like Medium, LinkedIn or Reddit, or a coupon and review section on a well known site. For years this ranking shortcut put affiliate content at the top of search results for competitive keywords like "best CBD gummies" or "best online casinos". Today it is one of the riskiest SEO tactics you can use.

⏱️ CHAPTERS 0:00 The ranking shortcut 0:22 What this video covers 0:35 What is parasite SEO? A simple definition 1:03 Why parasite SEO works: borrowed domain authority 1:38 Where parasite SEO happens: three common hosts 2:23 Parasite SEO at its peak: who ranked at the top 2:58 Google's crackdown: site reputation abuse policy timeline 4:07 What's allowed: where Google draws the line 4:50 Three risks of parasite SEO 5:23 The better path: build authority you own 5:51 How SERPsupport works 6:29 Get started

📌 WHAT YOU'LL LEARN

The definition of parasite SEO and where the name comes from. Like a parasite living on a host, your content feeds off a trusted domain's authority.
Why parasite SEO works: many Google ranking signals are tied to the website as a whole, so a brand new page on a strong domain inherits trust on day one, while a fresh website can need six to twelve months and hundreds of quality backlinks to compete.
The three most common types of parasite SEO: user-generated content platforms (Medium, LinkedIn articles, Reddit, Quora, free blogs), paid placements on big publishers (coupon sections, product review hubs, partner content), and black hat parasite SEO on hacked websites, abandoned university subdomains and expired pages, which can cross the line into illegal activity.
How affiliate marketers and publishers split commissions on parasite content, and why searchers ended up with results that looked trustworthy but lacked real expertise.
The full timeline of Google's response: the site reputation abuse policy announced in March 2024, manual actions starting in May 2024, the November 2024 clarification that first-party involvement or oversight is no excuse, the June 2026 spam update, and the August 2026 change in the European Economic Area.
What is still allowed: editorial guest posts written for a site's real readers, genuine forum answers, expertise shared on LinkedIn, and sponsored content that is clearly labeled with the rel="sponsored" link attribute.
The three big risks of relying on parasite SEO: you don't own the asset, one Google update can wipe out the entire section, and your brand gets tied to spammy tactics.
A safer, long-term link building strategy: earning relevant backlinks from real websites in your niche so authority flows to your own domain.

🔎 IS PARASITE SEO DEAD IN 2026? Not completely, but it is far riskier than it used to be. Google's site reputation abuse policy targets third-party content published mainly to exploit a host site's ranking signals, and Google has removed or demoted whole sections of major publishers. Since late August 2026 Google no longer applies site reputation abuse manual actions to search results in the European Economic Area, following pressure from the European Commission under the Digital Markets Act. However, Google says its algorithms can still treat an abusive section separately from the rest of the site, so it ranks on its own merits. In other words, the parasite SEO shortcut is not a safe strategy anywhere, including Europe.

🔗 THE BETTER ALTERNATIVE: EARN RELEVANT BACKLINKS Rankings you rent can be taken back at any moment. Rankings you build on your own website compound over time. The most durable way to grow organic traffic is to earn backlinks from relevant websites whose audience genuinely overlaps with yours. A link from a real site in your niche passes trust to your domain, not to someone else's, and every good link becomes part of an asset you keep. The hard part has always been outreach: finding relevant site owners, writing cold emails, and getting a reply.

🤝 ABOUT SERPSUPPORT SERPsupport.com is matchmaking for backlinks. Instead of cold email lists, shady link farms or renting someone else's reputation, you connect directly with relevant website owners who want to collaborate.

metadata.title: Google Just Dropped the Parasite SEO Penalty in Europe. Here's the Catch
metadata.author: Edward Sturm
metadata.shortDescription:
E1177: Google just changed how its parasite SEO penalty works across Europe, but the headline leaves out the most important part.

I break down Google’s change to its Site Reputation Abuse Policy inside the European Economic Area and explain what it means for parasite SEO, publishers, affiliate sites, and SEOs trying to rank through high-authority domains.

The European Commission challenged Google over its treatment of publisher sections containing sponsored, commercial, and third-party content. Google responded by changing how its manual site reputation abuse actions affect searchers inside the EEA.

As of August 30, the manual-action impact no longer applies to users searching from the European Economic Area, which includes the 27 EU countries plus Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein.

That sounds like a massive win for parasite SEO.

There’s a catch.

Google says it may separate the affected section of a website from the rest of the domain inside its ranking systems. That means a parasite section might avoid the manual penalty while also losing the authority it previously inherited from the host website.

In this episode:
- What parasite SEO means
- Why Reddit provides such a simple example of parasite SEO
- Why the EU challenged Google’s Site Reputation Abuse Policy
- What changed for searchers inside the European Economic Area
- Why the United States, United Kingdom, and other non-EEA markets still operate under the existing penalty system
- How Forbes Advisor became one of the clearest examples of publisher parasite SEO
- How Forbes ranked for commercial terms across insurance, finance, VPNs, home services, health, and other industries
- What happened after Google started enforcing its site reputation abuse rules
- Why removing the manual penalty does not mean parasite SEO gets a free pass
- How Google plans to separate third-party sections from the authority of the main domain
- Why subfolders and subdomains matter
- Why Forbes using forbes[.]com/advisor matters to this discussion
- Why Google’s section-level authority separation will determine how big this change really becomes
- Why the EEA search results may look very different from US and UK search results
- Why implementation will likely create unusual opportunities and inconsistencies
- What SEOs are saying about the change
- Why this matters more for publishers than social platforms like Reddit, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn

I also explain why the real SEO story here is not simply “Google stopped penalizing parasite SEO.”

The real question is whether Google successfully identifies commercial third-party sections and prevents those sections from inheriting the full ranking authority of the host domain.

If Google gets that right, the manual penalty matters a lot less.

If Google struggles with it, EEA search results could get very interesting.

I finish the episode with community reactions and my take on what SEOs need to watch next.

In episode 17, I cover some huge visibility drops for sites that are violating Google's 'Site reputation abuse' spam policy. For example, some prominent sites are dropping over time including some of the largest publishers on the web. Over time, Google seems to have algorithmically hit large publishers with affiliate sections of their sites, including Forbes, Fortune, CNN Underscored, WSJ Buyside, Marketwatch Guides, and more. It makes you wonder if Google is testing its 'Site reputation abuse' algorithm update, or if other changes are impacting those sections strongly...

metadata.author: The Agent Workshop
metadata.shortDescription:
Parasite SEO means ranking your page on a site Google already trusts. It can work in days, and it can get you penalized just as fast. This video covers what Google's site reputation abuse policy actually says, the four things Google checks in 2026, five safe ways to borrow authority (YouTube, Reddit, LinkedIn, Medium, real guest posts), the tricks that backfire, and a simple five-step plan.

Subscribe for a new AI build every week: https://www.youtube.com/@TheAgentWorkshop?sub_confirmation=1

4:05 Recap

Google spam policies (site reputation abuse): https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies#site-reputation-policy

More AI guides: https://artificialinteligenceai.com/

segments.text: There's a way to rank on Google in days, not months.
You publish on a site Google already trusts.
Since 2024, Google penalizes the wrong way to do it.
But five safe versions still work. Let's open the file.
Everything here comes from Google's own spam policy and SEO news coverage, checked October 1. It's a breakdown, not a promise of rankings.
Here's the idea. Google already trusts some sites, like big news sites, universities, and huge platforms.
You publish your page on one of those sites. A guest post, a sponsored section, a profile article, or a forum answer.
And it can rank in days instead of months, because Google trusts the host, not your own site.
The catch: when the page has nothing to do with the host, and nobody there really checks it, Google has a name for it. Site reputation abuse.
Here's how Google defines it.
Publishing third-party pages on a site to take advantage of the host site's ranking signals.

Google's own examples: an education site hosting payday loan reviews, a medical site hosting casino pages, a news site's coupon section run by an outside company, or a sports site hosting supplement reviews.
Google added this policy in March 2024.
In November 2024 it went further: using third-party content this way breaks the rules no matter how much the host is involved.
After that, big publishers got manual actions on those sections, as reported by Search Engine Journal.
So what does Google look for in 2026? Four signs that a section doesn't really belong to the site.
One: it looks different from the rest of the site.
Two: the quality is worse than the main site.
Three: there's no clear author.
And four: the same content shows up on other sites.

One new detail. Since August 30, inside the European Economic Area, Google separates those sections so they rank on their own, instead of a manual penalty. Everywhere else, manual actions still apply.
Now the good news. Borrowing authority still works when it's your own expertise, on platforms you actually belong to. Here are the five that work best.
One: YouTube. Videos show up right in Google results. Put the exact search phrase in your title and add chapters.
Two: Reddit. Write real, helpful answers in threads that already rank. Reddit shows up a lot in Google now.
Three: LinkedIn articles, for work and business topics, under your real name.
Four: Medium or Substack, for long, specific guides that link back to your site.
And five: guest posts on sites in your topic, where a real editor reviews what gets published.
And here's what gets you penalized.
Renting a folder or a subdomain on a big site for pages that have nothing to do with it.
Turnkey or white-label services that place pages for you. Google names these directly.
Pasting the same article across lots of sites.
And casino, payday loan, or coupon pages on sites that aren't about that.
On the other side, Google says wire stories, forum posts, closely edited content, and clearly labeled ads are fine.
Here's a safe version you can start today, in five steps.
One: pick one real search, like free live TV by country.
Two: search it, and note which Reddit, YouTube, or LinkedIn pages show up.
Three: answer it better on that same platform, under your name, with real steps or proof.

metadata.author: Ahrefs
metadata.shortDescription:
Google and AI have changed affiliate marketing. Websites are getting crushed. But this 20-year trail running site grew 249%. In this video, he shares his playbook. 

Additional resources: 
► https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CF3Uk2jc_ig
► Agent A: https://ahrefs.com/agent-a

Bryon Powell of iRunFar survived every ugly Google update and has continued climbing while everyone else sank.

We verify the numbers on camera, then walk through his operating system and learn how he's continuing to thrive. 

You'll learn: 
▸ The keys to Bryon's success, starting with "The Attention Dividend"
▸ The mental model that Bryon and his team use to manage their buyer's guides (best lists)
▸ The moat Bryon has over his competitors and how other affiliate sites can adopt this 
▸ Tips on how he can use AI to automate much of the work without losing quality

metadata.title: SaaS SEO Strategy - How I make $4,000/day with a SaaS
metadata.author: Vasco Aires
metadata.shortDescription:
This is my full SEO strategy as a SaaS founder - it's the exact tactics I'm using to grow our traffic (and revenue) from Google, Bing, and even ChatGPT and other LLM-based search engines.

I break down:
- How I’m turning every feature in my SaaS into evergreen traffic with SEO
- The three types of pages every SaaS should be creating
- Real examples from huge players like Canva, Veed, Thinkific, and Wise
- How to use SEO to steal traffic from your competitors by ranking for their brand names
- How LLMs like ChatGPT, Grok, and Perplexity pick up your site’s content, and how to make sure they recommend YOU instead of someone else
- How we use interactive tools, lead magnets, and dynamic content to improve conversions

Plus a behind-the-scenes look at how my tool, Arvow, automates a lot of this with AI (and how we’re building a new tool, Roverfy, to automate your product documentation) Whether you're new to SEO or already deep into SaaS growth, this is a no-fluff, real-world strategy you can start applying today.

metadata.title: How to Create Comparison Content (Without Making Your CEO Nervous): A Data Backed Approach
metadata.author: The Grow and Convert Marketing Show
metadata.shortDescription:
In this episode of the Grow and Convert Marketing Show, Devesh and Benji reveal why comparison keywords convert at a shocking 8.43%+ rate - and why most companies are afraid to target them.

We break down:
- Common objections from leadership teams that are hesitant to target these types of keywords
- Three practical approaches to creating comparison content without "trashing" competitors
- Examples of competitor and alternatives articles from companies like ClimbHire, Boken, and TapClicks

If you've been avoiding competitor keywords because they feel uncomfortable or unprofessional, this episode will show you how to approach them tastefully while capturing high-intent buyers already searching for alternatives.

Follow us at growandconvert.com/newsletter for articles and updates when new videos are released!

Helpful articles:
SEO conversion rates: https://www.growandconvert.com/conversion-rate-optimization/average-seo-conversion-rate/
Competitor comparison pages: https://www.growandconvert.com/seo/competitor-comparison-landing-pages/
SERP analysis: https://www.growandconvert.com/seo/how-to-do-serp-analysis/

Timestamps
[00:00:00] - Introduction to comparison keywords and high conversion rates
[00:01:00] - Explaining the situation: What happens when clients are uncomfortable with competitor content
[00:02:00] - Definition of comparison keywords (alternatives and versus keywords)
[00:03:50] - Data showing high conversion rates of comparison keywords (7.5%+)
[00:06:00] - Real-world examples of people searching for alternatives (DocuSign story)
[00:07:30] - Benji's personal example of searching for AI search monitoring alternatives
[00:08:30] - Common objections from clients/companies about mentioning competitors
[00:10:00] - Beginning of examples: How to create tasteful comparison content
[00:11:00] - First example: "Programs like Year Up" (Climb Hire) - minimal competitor mention approach
[00:14:00] - Second example: "Zola alternatives" (Boken) - slightly more comparative approach
[00:17:00] - Example of "backhanded compliments" in comparison content
[00:22:00] - Third example: "Clipfolio alternatives" (Tap Clicks) - more direct feature comparison
[00:25:00] - Strategies for convincing hesitant stakeholders to create comparison content
[00:27:00] - Showing SERPs to demonstrate competitors are already ranking
[00:28:00] - Final thoughts and alternative approaches if stakeholders remain hesitant
[00:29:00] - Closing

metadata.title: I Quit Affiliate SEO After 10 Years - Here's What I'm Doing Instead
metadata.author: SEO Jesus
metadata.shortDescription:
FREE Strategy Call to rank in 2026 on Google & LLMS: https://seojesus.com/oam-strategy-call/

In this video, Craig Campbell discusses the biggest SEO trends for 2026, which he anticipates will be "feeding the LLMs" (Large Language Models). He explains that since SEOs are losing traffic to informational searches on LLMs and AI overviews, they need to focus on putting their brands, businesses, products, and services into the LLMs to reclaim some of that traffic. He suggests that instead of focusing on one's own website with content-heavy approaches, the focus is now on being on established press websites or other platforms to feed the LLMs.

The conversation then turns to Campbell's reputation as a former affiliate marketer. He reveals that he is no longer doing affiliate marketing. He stopped doing Amazon affiliate marketing because the company continually cut commissions, making it an unprofitable venture, especially given the content-heavy websites he used to rely on.

Currently, Campbell's main focus is his own websites, specifically his e-commerce (ecom) stores, which provide the "real cash flow". He also does some paid media, works on personal branding (doing brand deals and influencer marketing), has ecom stores, works with SAS tools, and is involved in the iGaming niche. While brand deals are an added bonus, they are sporadic and not always consistent.

Campbell offers insights on e-commerce, stressing the importance of high profit margins and avoiding logistical pain points. He describes past failures, such as:

  * Trying to sell women's clothing, which had a 50% return rate.
  * Entering the e-cigarette niche, where advertising legal items was not possible.
  * Running an affiliate golf website where the average order value was only $20.
  * Learning from a friend whose ecom store selling wet wall panels struggled due to the high likelihood of the 2.4-meter-long panels breaking during delivery.

Finally, for someone looking to get into SEO in 2026 or simply trying to make money online, Campbell's advice is to focus on "productizing selling services". He suggests that the quickest path to making money is not ecom or building a brand, as those take years and can lead to giving up and getting a day job. A specific service he suggests is selling "listicles" related to feeding the LLM AI stuff. This is a low-barrier-to-entry service with high cash flow because it offers a valuable service to business owners, requires no inventory, and the service provider gets paid upfront. Once established, one can then add and scale other services. Campbell concludes that making money in SEO is hard now and that the old methods of cranking out content no longer work.

What are the best pay per call networks for rank and rent?
Pick by category and entry level. CallScaler Marketplace and Lead Smart take new publishers; eLocal only accepts publishers who already have call volume. My dashboard compares 23 of them.

The call has to last long enough (CallScaler says most offers want 60 to 120 seconds), arrive during the buyer's hours, and get through the hold period. Marketcall offers show a 7-day hold before a call is approved.

Search Google for "[your niche] pay per call" and "buy [your niche] calls", then search OfferVault filtered to Pay Per Call, then read eLocal's public rate card.

This is not theory. This is part of my real Beginner To 1K A Day journey, where I document the process of building online income step by step — the wins, the mistakes, the numbers, the strategy, and the lessons I learn along the way.

If you are interested in making money online, affiliate marketing, paid ads, Google Ads, lead generation, performance marketing, or building a real online business, this video will help you understand why Pay Per Call is one of the most underrated ways to generate income online.

In this video, you’ll learn:

How Pay Per Call affiliate marketing works  
How advertisers pay for qualified phone calls  
Why Marketcall can be a strong network for Pay Per Call offers  
How ROI works in paid advertising  
Why tracking and testing are important before scaling  
What beginners should understand before running paid traffic  
How one campaign can turn ad spend into profit when done correctly  

Pay Per Call is different from normal affiliate marketing because instead of waiting for someone to buy a product online, you can get paid when a qualified customer makes a phone call. That makes it a powerful model for people who want to learn affiliate marketing, lead generation, and paid ads.

My goal with this channel is simple: document the journey from beginner to $1K a day and share real lessons about making money online with Pay Per Call, affiliate marketing, Google Ads, landing pages, tracking, offers, and campaign optimization.

metadata.title: How to Find Pay Per Call Buyers | Build Performance Marketing Business | Pay Per Call University #9
metadata.author: ExclusiveLiveCall
metadata.shortDescription:
You understand Pay Per Call. You understand campaigns, routing, billing, payouts and profit.
Now it's time to start building the business.
In Episode 9 of Pay Per Call University, we answer one of the most important questions:
Where do you actually find buyers for your Pay Per Call campaigns?
But this episode introduces an even bigger idea.
Pay Per Call is performance marketing.
The agreement with the business owner can be simple:
We perform. You pay.
Think about going to a barber. You receive the haircut, then you pay for the service.
Performance marketing can follow a similar philosophy. Instead of asking a business owner to pay a large monthly marketing retainer and hope results eventually come, you can structure the relationship around an agreed measurable performance event.
Qualified Call → Pay Per Call
Lead → CPL
Qualified Opportunity → CPQ
Appointment → PPA
Acquisition → CPA
Sale → CPS
Revenue Generated → Revenue Share
The question becomes:
What performance does the business owner want to buy?
In Episode 9, you'll learn how to identify potential buyers, approach them, understand their customer-acquisition economics, offer a controlled test, and start building buyer coverage for your network.
In this episode, we cover:
- What performance marketing really means
- Why “We Perform. You Pay.” changes the sales conversation
- Direct buyers vs. networks and other demand partners
- How to choose your first vertical
- Where to find Pay Per Call buyers
- Google, Google Maps, LinkedIn, directories, events and direct outreach
- What makes a business a good buyer
- Why you should sell the economics, not just “leads”
- How to structure your first buyer conversation
- Starting with a controlled test
- Why depending on one buyer is dangerous
- How multiple local buyers can create nationwide coverage
- Using RTB to expand demand
- Using CRM to manage buyers, publishers, networks and prospects
- Using Market Intelligence to identify potential opportunities
- Automating buyer acquisition
- Using email, SMS and AI Voice outreach where appropriate
- How the same technology you provide your customers can help YOU acquire more customers
From Manual Prospecting to an Acquisition Machine
Finding buyers doesn't always have to mean searching for one contractor at a time.
With the ProAxis.ai ecosystem, the goal is to help performance marketers connect tools such as:
Market Intelligence → Data → Lead Enrichment → CRM → Automations → Email/SMS → Outreach AI → Interested Business Owner → Buyer → Campaign
That means the technology you're using to generate business for your customers can also help generate new customers for your own performance marketing company.
And Calls Are Only the Beginning
As we continue through Pay Per Call University, we're going far beyond phone calls.
We'll explore:
Lead Form Builder
Lead Ping/Post & RTB
Consent Certificates
Lead Enrich™
Lead Vault™
Intent Leads™
Visitor Reveal™
Audience Builder™
Intent Watch™
Lead Exchange™
CRM
Market Intelligence
Automations
Outreach AI
AI Voice
and much more.
The bigger goal is to teach you how to build a complete performance marketing business.
And as you grow, the ProAxis ecosystem can also create opportunities to buy or sell qualified call traffic, depending on available supply, campaigns and demand.
Pay Per Call University is completely FREE.
Learn the business first.
Then, when you're ready to build what we're teaching:
ProAxis.ai
Next Episode
In Episode 10, we're leaving theory behind and getting into the nitty-gritty:
How to Build & Launch a Pay Per Call Campaign — From Buyer to Live Traffic
We'll take the buyer we found in Episode 9 and turn:
“I'm interested.”
into:
“Send me calls.”
#PayPerCall #PayPerCallUniversity #ProAxis #PerformanceMarketing #LeadGeneration #AffiliateMarketing #PayPerLead #CallTracking #RTB #VoiceAI #MarketingAutomation

👉 Get RHIMS 10 ($27 until Nov 8, then $47): https://bensbonusoffers.netlify.app/go/rhims-10/yt

Pay-per-call affiliate marketing for beginners: a plumber pays $30, a roofer $50, a lawyer $100 and more for one qualified phone call, and the affiliate who sent the call stays off the phone. RHIMS 10: Get Paid Per Call by JayKay Dowdall is a course about getting those calls with free traffic, and this RHIMS 10 review is filmed inside the members area after going through all 16 lessons.

What the course teaches: you register the just-expired domain of a closed local service business, rebuild its homepage with AI as a clearly disclosed referral page, host it free on GitHub Pages, put a $10 local tracking number with a press-1 greeting on it, validate real callers, then sell the calls to a pay-per-call network that pays weekly. The video shows the roadmap, the networks (eLocal, MarketCall, RingPartner) and how to read an offer card, the research on ExpiredDomains.net and the Wayback Machine, the AI rebuild with three prompts, the $10 Call Stack on NumberBarn, the vendor bonuses (Niche Hit List, Free Traffic Treasure Map, Case Files) and the real case file numbers: 165 visitors, 9 calls, 3 paid at $55, about $34 in costs.

Then my three bonuses, built new for this launch: the Call Funnel Domain Scout (a Chrome extension that checks a whole ExpiredDomains.net page against the Wayback Machine and scores every domain), the Network Approval Kit (evidence pack, application answers, onboarding-call cheat sheet, pay-bump email) and the Call Funnel Portfolio Tracker (Google Sheet with the keep-or-kill, apply and pay-bump rules built in).

Price: $27 one-time during launch week (Nov 3-8, 2026), $47 after. Upgrades are optional: Fresh List $60 for 12 months, Masterclass Replay $97, RHIMS Vault $197. Beyond the course you pay for a domain (about $10-15 a year) and a NumberBarn number (about $10 plus $6.99 a month). Fits beginners and affiliates who want an evergreen model without content, ads or an audience.

Terms used in this video:
• Pay-per-call: affiliate marketing where a business pays per qualified phone call instead of per sale.
• Qualified call: a call that meets the buyer's rules (intent, minimum length, location, hours).
• Call funnel: a website whose job is to make a visitor call one tracking number.
• Expired domain: a domain whose owner let the registration lapse, available to register again.
• Tracking number: a phone number you own that logs every call and forwards it (here via NumberBarn).
• Pay-per-call network: the middleman (eLocal, MarketCall, RingPartner) that routes calls to buyers and pays affiliates weekly.
• Pay bump: a higher payout per call, asked for after a track record of qualified calls.

metadata.title: What is a Server-to-Server (S2S) Postback? | Everflow Mini Webinars
metadata.author: Everflow - Partner Marketing Platform
metadata.shortDescription:
🚀 Mastering Server-to-Server (S2S) Postbacks for Accurate Attribution
Are you tired of losing track of your conversions due to ad blockers, cookie restrictions, or browser privacy updates? In this Everflow Mini Webinar, we dive deep into Server-to-Server (S2S) Postbacks—the gold standard for secure and reliable conversion tracking.

🔍 What You’ll Learn:
The Basics of S2S: What exactly is a server-to-server call and how does it differ from traditional pixel tracking?

The Power of Transaction IDs: Discover why the Transaction ID (TID) is the single most important piece of data in your marketing ecosystem.

The S2S Workflow: A step-by-step breakdown of how data moves from a user click to the advertiser’s CRM and back to Everflow for 100% attribution.

Real-World Use Cases: * E-commerce: Tracking sales across different browsers and ad blockers.

Finance & CRM: Managing long-term conversion cycles in platforms like Salesforce and HubSpot.

Mobile Apps: Integrating with MMPs (Mobile Measurement Partners) like Adjust and Branch for seamless app-install tracking.

🛠 Why Switch to S2S Postbacks?
Unlike client-side pixels, S2S postbacks offer:

Enhanced Accuracy: No more "missing" conversions caused by cookie limitations.

Greater Security: Data is passed directly between servers, reducing the risk of fraud.

Future-Proofing: Reliable tracking that works independently of browser privacy settings (like ITP).

📽 Video Chapters:
0:00 - Introduction to S2S Postbacks 0:21 - Why Use S2S Over Pixels? 0:37 - The S2S Postback Process Explained 1:08 - The Role of the Transaction ID 1:17 - Use Case 1: E-commerce & Influencer Marketing 1:43 - Use Case 2: Finance, CRM, & Long-Term Tracking 2:08 - Use Case 3: Mobile Apps & MMP Integration

🔗 About Everflow
Everflow is the leading partner marketing platform that helps businesses scale their performance through better tracking, automation, and analytics.

Ready to level up your tracking? 👉 Visit Everflow.io to learn more. 👉 Subscribe for more Mini Webinars on performance marketing!

### Explore the Resources
➡️ For detailed guides visit the Everflow Helpdesk: https://helpdesk.everflow.io/
➡️ New to Everflow? Visit our website: https://www.everflow.io/

#PerformanceMarketing #S2SPostbacks #Everflow #AdTech #ConversionTracking #AffiliateMarketing #DigitalMarketingTips

metadata.shortDescription:
🚀 How to Set Up & Test Your Advertiser Postback in Everflow
Master the technical foundations of conversion tracking with this deep dive into Advertiser Postbacks. In this mini-webinar, we explore the critical mechanisms that allow advertiser servers to signal successful conversion events—like purchases, sign-ups, or app installs—directly back to Everflow.

📝 What You’ll Learn:
The Postback Mechanism: Understand how the unique transaction ID generated during the initial click serves as the vital link between a conversion event and the original partner, offer, and click.

Setup Workflow: A step-by-step guide to ensuring your partner tracking links successfully pass transaction ID macros to the advertiser's system.

Configuration Essentials: How to accurately configure postback URLs within the Global Postback section or specific offer settings.

Validation & Testing: Learn how to use the Advertiser Postback Report as your primary diagnostic tool to verify signal reception, variable processing (sales, amounts), and conversion status (approved vs. rejected).

💡 Real-World Use Cases Covered:
E-commerce & Retail: Ensuring accurate sale value recording for high-volume holiday campaigns using amount=sale_value parameters.

B2B SaaS: Integrating CRM systems (like Salesforce) for late-stage conversions (e.g., "Opportunity Closed/Won") occurring 45+ days after the initial lead.

Mobile App Growth: Setting up postbacks with MMPs (Mobile Measurement Partners) like Singular to map internal tokens to Everflow transaction IDs.

Budget Management: Using Caps at the offer, partner, or group level to adhere to advertiser budgets and capacity constraints.

🛠 Tools Mentioned:
Everflow Advertiser Postback Report

Transaction ID Macros

Server-to-Server (S2S) Postbacks

MMP Integrations (Singular)

CRM Integrations (Salesforce)

Everflow is the leading partner marketing platform for managing, tracking, and optimizing every performance channel in one place.

metadata.title: Tracking & Conversion Domain Management | Webinars
metadata.author: Everflow - Partner Marketing Platform
metadata.shortDescription:
### **Mastering Tracking & Conversion Domains in Everflow**

Unlock the full potential of your performance marketing campaigns by mastering tracking and conversion domain management in Everflow. In this comprehensive webinar, Everflow Customer Success Manager Isaac Maier walks you through the essentials of setting up, managing, and reporting on your domains to ensure accurate tracking, build brand trust, and optimize performance.

Whether you're new to the Everflow platform or looking to refine your current setup, this session provides actionable insights and a live platform demonstration. Learn how to leverage custom domains for specific partners and offers, analyze their performance with powerful reporting tools, and get a first look at upcoming features designed to keep your campaigns running smoothly.

**TIMESTAMPED AGENDA:**
* `00:00` - Webinar Introduction
* `01:05` - Meet the Presenter: Isaac Maier
* `01:45` - Intro to Domains: Tracking vs. Conversion Domains
* `02:19` - How to Set Up Your Domains with Everflow
* `03:20` - Platform Demo: Finding Your Domain Configurations
* `04:11` - Understanding Primary Tracking & Conversion Domains
* `05:06` - Assigning Domains for Specific Partners and Offers
* `05:25` - Platform Demo: Setting an Offer-Specific Tracking Domain
* `06:41` - Platform Demo: Setting a Partner-Specific Tracking Domain
* `08:12` - Reporting on Domain Performance
* `08:25` - Platform Demo: Using Flex & Dynamic Nested Reports for Domains
* `09:44` - Upcoming Feature Preview: Traffic Pulse
* `10:53` - Everflow Pay: Streamlining Partner Payments
* `12:21` - What's Next: Upcoming Everflow Events
* `12:52` - Q&A

### Explore the Resources

➡️ For a more detailed guides visit the Everflow Helpdesk: `https://helpdesk.everflow.io/`  
➡️ New to Everflow? Visit our website to learn more: `https://www.everflow.io/`

#Everflow #AffiliateMarketing #DomainManagement #PerformanceMarketing #TrackingDomains #MarTech #SaaS #AdTech #Webinar #ConversionTracking

metadata.title: High-Ticket Affiliate Marketing for Beginners: 5-Step System & Costly Mistakes
metadata.author: Smart Capital
metadata.shortDescription:
Want to earn bigger commissions from affiliate marketing without chasing hundreds of tiny sales? This video breaks down high-ticket affiliate marketing for beginners into a clear 5-step system: choosing a profitable niche, finding legitimate high-ticket affiliate programs, building trust with a small audience, warming up cold traffic, and turning one sale into a meaningful commission.

You will learn how high-ticket affiliate marketing actually works, how commissions are structured (flat bounties, percentage payouts, and recurring SaaS commissions), which niches pay best in 2026, and how long the sales cycle really takes. We also cover the beginner mistakes that quietly kill most new affiliates: promoting products they do not understand, skipping the funnel, chasing commission rates instead of buyer trust, and expecting fast results from a model built on longer research and decision cycles.

Whether you are starting from zero or switching from low-ticket products, this guide gives you a realistic, step-by-step framework for affiliate marketing income, side hustle earnings, and building an online business the honest way. No hype, no guaranteed income claims, just the system, the numbers, and the pitfalls to avoid.

https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLdqSR1MFEl_s
#HighTicketAffiliateMarketing #AffiliateMarketingForBeginners #AffiliateMarketing2026 #SmartCapital #MakeMoneyOnline #PassiveIncome #SideHustle #OnlineBusiness #AffiliatePrograms #DigitalMarketing #WorkFromHome #EarnMoneyOnline

TIMESTAMPS:
00:00 — Intro: one sale, $500 in commission
01:13 — What it is: high-ticket vs low-ticket affiliate marketing
02:40 — Real programs: web hosting — Kinsta pays $50–$500 per referral
03:29 — E-commerce platforms: Shopify reported up to $2,000 per sale
03:44 — Course platforms: Kajabi and Teachable pay 30% recurring
03:54 — Marketing software: ClickFunnels 40% recurring, Semrush ~$200
04:07 — Freelance and lead generation: Fiverr $15–$150 per buyer
05:06 — The honest earnings math: ten sales a month
06:58 — Beginner promotion playbook: reviews, comparisons, tutorials, SEO
08:42 — Common mistakes: untested products, spam, quitting early
09:56 — The FTC disclosure requirement: disclose every affiliate link
11:07 — Recap: the five numbers worth writing down

Disclaimer: This video is for educational purposes only and is not financial advice. Always do your own research or consult a licensed financial advisor before making financial decisions.

segments.text: Right now, pages built on a loophole are ranking number one on Google,
and they are hosted on Google's own website.
This isn't a hack, it's a loophole.
And right now, the whole SEO world is talking about it.
But here is the catch. It doesn't last.
So, let's look at what's really going on and if you really need to invest your time,
money, and energy into it.
So, grab your coffee.
Hi, and welcome to the SEO Coffee Mornings with me, Alek Borisov.
Yesterday I have promised that we are going to talk about Google's September update.
Well, the strangest thing happened during it.
A grey-hat loophole took off right as that update rolled out.
Today I will explain what it is, why it's working,
and how to weigh it up as someone building a real business.
So let's go. First, the idea behind it, it's called parasite SEO.
I've been doing that for more than a decade.
And I really think that you shouldn't.
Instead of ranking your own website,
you publish your content on a big trusted website and borrow its authority.
Think of a guest post on a huge news site that ranks the next day.
The host has years of trust with Google, and your page rides on that trust.
Parasite SEO isn't new, and not all of it is against the rules.
A genuine guest post on a real site is fine.
What's new in the scale of what people are doing right now is the amount of pages
that can be built. Here is the loophole everyone's talking about.
Google has a tool for developers called Google Apps Script.
Among other things, it can publish a web page on Google's own domain,
script.google.com, and Google's own domain is about as trusted as a website as you can get.
So, people started publishing pages, and some of them went straight to the top of Google.
The timing is striking.
This took off at the exact time as Google's September update,
the one we covered yesterday.
Pages for all kinds of searches, in many languages,
suddenly ranking on Google's own platform.
So why is this happening right now?
Two reasons.
One, Google's own pages carry so much trust that they get found and indexed fast.
Two, Google has eased off one kind of enforcement.
By the end of August,
Google stopped applying the manual penalties for what it calls site reputation abuse
for searchers in Europe.
That was to settle a European Commission investigation.
Google says it still stands by the policy,
but many in the industry feel enforcement has gone quieter while Google's
attention shifts to AI. So, the door is open wider than usual, at least for now.
Now, an important detail.
It is the reason this isn't a simple white-hat tactic or something that a regular
Joe can implement. Many of these pages use a technique called cloaking.
Google's own rulebook defines cloaking as showing one thing to Google and a
different thing to the visitor to manipulate the ranking.
So, Google sees a normal article,
but the real person gets sent straight to an affiliate offer or a page of ads or
a product or service that he is providing or partnering with.
That breaks the Google rules,
and the security researchers have already flagged these Apps Script pages as a
phishing and malware risk.
Just so we are clear, this episode is about what is happening, not how to do it.
Is it worth it?
So, I've said that I had previous experience with parasite SEO,
especially in the beginning of my SEO career,
in the long early days of Pandas and Penguins and Hummingbirds.
And I really think that by looking at the time that have passed,
I have spent my money, time, and energy on the wrong thing by chasing some of these,
because in the meantime, you can invest in a real business.
And why is that? Because here's the honest math.
The pages rank for hours, not months.
They spike, they fade. Sometimes you can keep them for days, sometimes for a week.
And you have to invest in them in order for them to stay on the top.
You have to put the work and the money, and it turns into a treadmill,
and your focus is diluted, and the pages live on an account that Google can suspend.
So you don't really own any of that.
It's not an asset. Now think about it like an entrepreneur, as you probably are.
Your time, your money, your focus are limited.
You can spend them renting traffic that's gone by this afternoon.
Or you can spend them building an asset of your own,
one that keeps earning and that you could one day sell, for example.
Or you can focus on your client's work.
So you may not get the cash right now, but in the long run,
you'll be far more profitable investing into an actual asset.
These are two different games to play.
So your action for this day, and it's a simple one.
Protect your own brand and the brand of your clients, your product names.
Open a private browser window right now and search for your brand name,
plus words like review, login, discount,
anything that's related to your business or your client's business.
Look for any page on a
script.google.com that are using your name or sending people somewhere shady,
because people may brandjack your terms.
They can get your brand name and hijack people and turn them into something else,
and that's not okay.
If you find one pretending to be you or your brand or your product or your service
or your client's service or product, report it to Google.
It takes five minutes, and it protects the brand you're actually building.
That's today's cup.
Subscribe so it lands in your feed, and tell me in the comments,
have you spotted one of these Google-hosted pages on your own searches?
Drop the keyword below.
Today's last drop. Thousands of years ago, Aesop told this story of a tortoise and hare.
The hare was so sure he'd win that he raced ahead.
He sprinted, and then he stopped to rest.
The slow, steady tortoise just kept going and crossed the line first.
The lesson we still repeat today is that slow and steady wins the race.
The fast feels good for a moment,
but what you actually have to do is run for a marathon.
Race is won by those who can sustain for a long periods of time their tempo.
Build your real asset. Be a tortoise.
That's the last drop. See you tomorrow morning, and bye from me.

segments.text: Search Google for a product recommendation, and you will often find a Reddit discussion in the results.
Here is an actual search for the best time tracking software for freelancers.
A Reddit comparison appears among the organic results.
That creates an opportunity: help someone on a page they are already discovering through search.
The tool linked in the description can find relevant discussions and offers Autopilot to write and publish
comments on your behalf.
We will start with the strategy, then build the workflow and write one comment manually.
First, there is a distinction that will save you from chasing the wrong kind of Reddit traffic.
Reddit parasite SEO means using a third party discussion as a place where people can discover your useful
contribution.
The thread is the page Google displays.
Your comment is one contribution inside that page.
It still needs to be relevant, visible and helpful.
Dropping a product name does not automatically give your website a ranking.
There is another route.
AI Overviews can link to Reddit discussions as supporting sources.
This earlier capture shows a Reddit citation for the same kind of search.
It does not mean Google will cite your comment or recommend your product.
We will treat search results and AI citations as separate observations, with a date attached.
We will cover two practical routes.
One is finding an existing search visible thread and contributing something useful where replies are allowed.
The other is publishing an original Reddit post that answers a real search question.
That second route needs its own evidence and community permission.
Neither route comes with a guaranteed Google position.
Our example is a time tracking product for freelancers, rather than a generic marketing niche.
You will see actual search evidence, real discussions, a keyword map, the tool setup, a manual comment and a
separate original post outline.
By the end, you will have a repeatable process and know exactly when to skip an opportunity.
Start with the person behind the query.
A freelancer searching for a time tracker might need to record billable work, explain an invoice, or replace a
platform tracker.
Those are different jobs.
We will focus on people who need clear client work records, because that gives us a reason to help beyond
mentioning an app.
The journey has several steps.
A person searches, opens a discussion, reads an answer and may investigate a product.
Traffic can disappear at any of those steps.
A ranking thread can have a buried comment.
A visible comment can get no clicks.
A click can bring the wrong person.
We will measure those separately.
Even when you do not comment, the discussion can improve your marketing.
Notice the language people use, what alternatives they have tried, and what makes a workflow fail.
A request for exportable client records is more specific than time tracking.
That detail can shape your reply, your website and the examples in your documentation.

metadata.title: How to build AEO Comparison Pages For AI Dominance
metadata.author: CXL
metadata.shortDescription:
In AI search, comparison pages are your unfair advantage.

LLMs love them because they make reasoning easier. 

They don’t need to crawl ten separate pages to compare features. 

A well-structured comparison page hands the answer over on a silver platter.

Steve Toth explains it in this clip:

- Two- and three-way comparison pages outperform generic listicles.
- Pages that compare specific features for specific ICPs (like 'Asana vs ClickUp for SEO agencies') are the ones models cite most often.
- Adding recency, like 'June 2025', helps because LLMs weigh freshness in their ranking logic.

The result?

You don’t just show up alongside competitors, you become the source even for your competitors’ mentions inside AI answers.

This is what Steve walks through step-by-step in his CXL course on Answer Engine Optimization - how to build a scalable comparison page system that dominates AI search visibility.

Sign up here: https://cxl.com/institute/live-course/optimize-pages-for-ai-search-with-aeo-cohort/

#SEO #GEO #Marketing #B2B

metadata.title: SEO in 2026: How I'd Rank in Google in the AI Era
metadata.author: Ahrefs
metadata.shortDescription:
SEO in 2026 has evolved, and here is exactly how I’d rank in Google in the AI era before your clicks disappear.

Additional Resources:
► https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xsVTqzratPs
► https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6NFei1FbytM
► https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gReszNnykpg

Last year flipped the table. Traffic slid, panic spiked, and AI Overviews started siphoning clicks like crazy. Our fresh data shows that when an AI Overview appears, the top result now loses around 58% of its clicks. In this video, I break down the 3 shifts reshaping search that explain what actually works now. We start with modern discovery, because your buyers do not rely on one page or one platform anymore. They bounce from Google to Reddit to YouTube to review sites, then validate on Amazon. AI assistants are doing the same thing, pulling from YouTube, Reddit, forums, publishers, and niche sites. With 86% of top-cited sources unique to each assistant, you have to reverse engineer your niche. I show you how to use Ahrefs Brand Radar to open the Cited Domains report so you can see exactly which websites AI assistants cite, and where you and your competitors get mentioned.

Then we get into query fan-out and why brand is everything. AI takes a single prompt like best smartphone for photography, explodes it into dozens of sub-queries like vs, best, top, review, alternative, then stitches an answer from the pages ranking for those terms. If your brand is mentioned across those pages, your odds of inclusion go way up. Our research shows branded mentions correlate with AI Overview visibility more than backlinks, referring domains, or Domain Rating. I walk you through finding the right pages in Brand Radar’s Cited Pages report, filtering for predictable fan-out patterns, and getting your product reviewed or added to high-impact lists and comparisons without wasting time on pages that will never move the needle.

Finally, we talk about where traditional SEO still wins because organic clicks are flowing to action. AI can explain concepts, but it cannot complete the task. Queries like backlink checker, mortgage calculator, or snow removal service need a click. I show you a quick workflow to surface action-driven keywords at scale using a keyword research tool, the Matching Terms report, Include filters like calculator, checker, generator, and the Intents filter to pull transactional terms. This is where content, links, and technical SEO still work like a charm in 2026.

If you are planning your roadmap for the year, you cannot afford to guess. Watch now to see the exact playbook I’d use to be discoverable everywhere, win AI citations, and capture the action-driven clicks your competitors are sleeping on. segments.text: Last year, SEO fundamentally changed.
Traffic was down across the board.
People were in full-on panic mode. Some
even pivoted to new professions. Sites
that had ranked for years were bleeding
out. But worse than the losses was the
uncertainty. No one knew what was coming
or if SEO even had a future. And the
data's brutal. Our research from April
showed that when an AI overview appears
in search results, the number one
ranking page loses about 35% of its
clicks. And we just reran that study and
it's now a 58% loss. But what's changed
is that we finally have some answers
because last year's turmoil revealed
three key shifts in search behavior that
give us hints into where SEO may be
going. And it all starts by
understanding how discovery works today.
So, I bought these headphones about a
month ago and I started on Google. I
searched for best headphones, clicked on
a few listicles, jotted down some common
models, and I didn't actually read a
thing. But I went to Reddit to see what
people were saying about those models.
Then I hit YouTube to watch dedicated
reviews and comparisons. And when I
finally went to the store to pick one
up, I was reading Amazon reviews on my
phone just to make sure I was making the
right purchase. This buying journey
might sound exhaustive, [music] but it's
not unusual. Information has never been
more accessible and we've been
researching like this for years. And
while this might not seem like it has
anything to do with SEO, it has [music]
everything to do with it because AI
assistants are learning the same way we
do. They're researching YouTube, Reddit,
forums, review sites, and using all of
it to decide who to recommend. In fact,
86% of the top cited sources are unique
to each AI assistant. Google AI
overviews lean heavily on YouTube,
Reddit, and Quora. ChatGPT prefers
publishers and news outlets and
Perplexity tends to cite niche and
regional sites. But that doesn't mean
getting mentioned on these domains will
automatically put you in AI overviews
because every niche and topic is
different. [music] So, to see the
websites being mentioned in your niche,
you need to reverse engineer the
competition. Just go to Ahrefs Brand
Radar with your brand and your
competitors' brand set, then open the
cited domains report. From here, you can
see the exact websites AI assistants are
citing in the queries where you and your
competitors are mentioned. But showing
up on these domains isn't enough. AI
pulls from specific pages and the pages
it chooses to cite is all based on the
second shift. Brand is everything. When
you type something like best smartphone
for photography into an AI assistant, it
doesn't just spit out an answer from
memory. [music] It fans that single
query out into dozens of smaller
subqueries. Things like iPhone 17 Pro
versus Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra camera,
best phone for low-light photos,
smartphone with best zoom lens in 2026.
Then it pulls information from the pages
that rank for each of these subqueries
and stitches it all together into one
answer. This is called query fanout and
it's how most AI assistants work. So, if
your brand is mentioned across the pages
that rank for those subqueries, you have
a much better chance of being included
in the final response. In fact, our
research shows that branded mentions
have the strongest correlation with
visibility in Google's AI overviews.

and domain rating. To find the right
pages to get mentioned on, go to Ahrefs
Brand Radar, enter your brand, your
competitors, and your niche, then open
the cited pages report. Add a filter
where the query contains words like
best, top, versus, review, or
alternative. And these are the
predictable fanout queries AI tends to
use. Now you have a list of the exact
pages worth getting mentioned on, which
will mostly be list roundups, comparison
posts, and dedicated reviews. Reach out
to the authors and try to get your
product reviewed there. Send them free
samples or do whatever you need to to
get your mention there. But here's the
thing, even if you get mentioned on AI
overviews and different chatbots,
there's still a massive chunk of search
where traditional SEO still wins. And
that's the third shift. Organic clicks
are flowing to action. Here's the deal.
Google's AI search is still very much in
its formative years.
>> [music]
>> It's great at answering questions,
summarizing large amounts of content,
and providing decent recommendations.
But it can't really do anything
meaningful for you. Not yet at least.
Like when someone searches backlink
checker, snow removal service, or
mortgage calculator, Google or any
chatbot isn't going to satisfy that
query with information alone because
that's not what people want. They're
looking to complete an action. Now,
compare that to informational queries
like what is a mortgage? AI overview.
How to calculate BMI? AI overview. What
is compound interest? AI overview.
That's why AI overviews don't really
exist for these types of action-driven
queries because Google knows the user
needs to click somewhere or decide
something to get what they want. And
that's ultimately the goal of Google,
deliver the best result for any given
query. This is where traditional SEO,
content, links, and technical still work
like a charm. So, if there's one thing
you must do before you target a query,
is answer this question. Can AI fully
satisfy the user for this query? If the
answer is no and the query has value for
your business, you really need to
consider targeting the traditional way.
Now, if you already have a list of
keywords, go through them and ask
yourself that question. But if you want
to find these opportunities in bulk, you
can do that with a neat little trick in
the keyword research tool. Just enter
broad seeds related to your niche, then
head to the matching terms report. Add
an include filter with modifiers like
calculator, checker, generator, and
more. These will all be action-oriented
queries because they're for free tools.
So, the typical content and links game
should still be valid here. Now, if
tools aren't your thing, another quick
way to find queries that will likely get
organic clicks is to filter for
transactional queries. All you have to
do is choose transactional in the
intense filter and you'll have a list of
queries that people search when they
want to transact or do something. SEO
has changed, no doubt. The main thing
being that you need to be discoverable
everywhere. Focus on building a brand
that gets mentioned on important pages
like lists, comparisons, review sites,
and social media all while remembering
that the fundamentals of SEO, yes, the
old version, isn't dead. The game hasn't
ended. You just need to split your
attention into these three buckets and
adapt to search with searchers as their
behavior changes.
